findings.summary: Pre-existing accessibility defect found by the first native run: the Add Expense sheet's wrapping Pressable is an accessibility element by default, so iOS exposes the whole sheet (keypad, Save, chips) as ONE element ("Discard draft, Type, Scan, Close, $0.00, ...") and VoiceOver users cannot reach the keys or Save individually. Fixed with accessible={false} on that wrapper, failing-first Jest test added.
findings.source: TS-QA-103 spike, simulator accessibility hierarchy dump, 2026-11-23

findings.summary: The accessibility-collapse defect in sheets (default-accessible Pressable/TouchableOpacity wrapping a sheet makes iOS expose it as ONE element). FIXED everywhere in the app: panels opt out (accessible={false}, focusable={false}) in the shared Sheet, Add Expense (sheet + date picker), CategoryPickerField, ExpensesScreen edit sheet, ExpenseItemsViewSheet, EditGroupExpenseModal; the two wrapping overlays SimpleSelect and TypeaheadInput; and every backdrop is a non-accessible element (7 wrapping + 7 childless sibling backdrops, incl. CardPicker, ExpenseDetail, GroupSettings, SettleUp, invite, create-group, TagPicker). ENFORCED by a source contract test (sheetAccessibility.test.ts, 48 cases) that scans every backdrop/panel, so a new one cannot regress it. DEVICE-VERIFIED on the iOS 27 simulator (failing first where noted): Add Expense sheet, shared Sheet (group picker), CategoryPickerField (flow failed before the fix: 'Food & Drink' unreachable; passes after), date-picker sheet, SimpleSelect (Insights 'Analyse'). NOT device-verified (same one-prop pattern, contract-enforced only): ExpensesScreen edit sheet, ExpenseItemsViewSheet, EditGroupExpenseModal, TypeaheadInput, and the sibling-backdrop sheets. A first attempt that LABELED the backdrops as 'Dismiss' buttons made it worse (the tree held only that node), caught on the simulator and reverted; the contract now forbids labels/roles on backdrops.

Sign-in keyboard covered the password field and Sign in button. FIXED with useScrollToEndOnKeyboard (scrolls the bottom-anchored form on keyboardDidShow), unit-tested (3 cases). DEVICE-VERIFIED: the sign-in subflow no longer dismisses the keyboard between fields and every flow still signs in. Register/ForgotPassword have the same pattern to a lesser degree (see F-011); on very short viewports the hook may scroll the email field out of view (F-010).

UI review: on Android a Pressable with accessible={false} may still be a TalkBack focus stop because focusable defaults to true. FIXED: focusable={false} added next to accessible={false} on the shared Sheet and the Add Expense sheet wrapper, with test assertions. Real TalkBack behaviour is still unverified (no Android run yet).

UI review: the Add Expense keypad keys, now individually reachable, had no button role and glyph-only names for backspace and decimal point. FIXED: accessibilityRole=button and labels 'Delete' / 'Decimal point', with a test.

Sheets could not be dismissed with VoiceOver's two-finger Z. FIXED: every sheet has onAccessibilityEscape wired to the same close path as its backdrop/close button, on an ANCESTOR of its content (the Add sheet's handler first sat on a sibling backdrop and could never fire: F-007). Enforced by the contract test. The gesture itself cannot be driven by Maestro and was NOT exercised on a device.

Security review: validate_database_url was bypassable (libpq query parameters dbname/hostaddr/service/options/HOST, comma multi-host netloc, newline, unicode digits), so 'cannot be pointed at production' was not enforced. FIXED: one strict anchored fullmatch pattern with no query string; 25 hostile inputs added to the unit tests.

Security review: throwaway Postgres used trust auth on loopback TCP with a predictable /tmp work dir (co-tenant risk on shared hosts). FIXED: scram-sha-256 with a per-run password, mktemp -d work dir (0700), database URL passed by environment not argv, PYTHONSAFEPATH, empty HOME; verified live.

Security review P3 batch, all FIXED: Python app-URL regex looser than JS (now compiled from the single source with fullmatch and ASCII digits); state file API URL/secret unvalidated (now validated); bootstrap/provision not dotenv-disabled and pydantic env_file re-read after chdir (prelude now covers every command and sets env_file=None; control run proves the leak without it); stop script sourced the state file, loose path pattern, unverified PID (now grep-parsed, strict path regex, PID identity check); rename blind spot in the scope diff (--no-renames); in-place native builds outside CI refused; android-emulator-runner pinned by commit SHA; checkout persist-credentials false; keyless push/FX URLs blackholed.

Security review, accepted: uploaded CI artifacts can contain per-flow synthetic user passwords (Maestro argv/log); those users exist only in a disposable database destroyed at teardown, and the JWT secret and state files are not uploaded. Evidence tamper-resistance is self-referential (evidence sits beside the artifact): it catches accidental drift, not a hostile writer. Documented, not changed.

waiver.reason: Synthetic credentials for a destroyed disposable database; artifact evidence is a drift check by design.

findings.summary: Code review: build-android.sh piped unzip into grep -q under pipefail, so a correct APK could fail the build with SIGPIPE (AC-004 could never go green). FIXED: bundle extracted to a temp file first.
Code review: the workflow concurrency group for non-PR runs could replace a pending main run, losing the regression jobs the release gate needs. FIXED: non-PR runs use github.run_id; a test pins it.

Code review: the group-expense server check did not verify the direction of the debt, and expense-create never checked the amount. FIXED: guest->me transfer of exactly 15.00 and no transfer from the viewer; cost 12.50 compared as exact decimals; live check shows 12.51 is rejected.

Code review P3 batch, FIXED: orphan API on health timeout; run.sh eval masking installer failure; run_flows lost results on an exception/timeout (now per-flow try/except, incremental summary, per-flow timeout); login pacing counted at flow start (now at flow end); regression suite excluded smoke flows (now includes them) and CI did not shuffle (now does); job-name contract and release-gate main() glue untested (now tested); keypad ids hard-coded in the selector test (now derived from the app) and comments satisfying it (now requires a real testID attribute); Maestro flows not treated as tests by test_integrity (now are); docs gaps for verification.md and definition-of-done. Left as is: draft-recovery relies on waitForAnimationToEnd (passed in 7 of 7 runs; follow-up if it flakes), ScreenHeader ids derive from titles (stable for the five tab roots).

UI review: the Add Expense sheet's escape handler was on a sibling backdrop, never an ancestor of its content, so the VoiceOver gesture could not reach it. FIXED: handler moved to the modal root; contract test asserts it.

UI review: SimpleSelect (TouchableOpacity backdrop wrapping the sheet) and TypeaheadInput (absoluteFill Pressable wrapping the dropdown) still had the collapsing-ancestor bug. FIXED (accessible={false} + escape); SimpleSelect device-verified via the Insights 'Analyse' picker, TypeaheadInput contract-enforced only.
UI review: seven childless sibling backdrops were empty accessible elements with no escape handler. FIXED (accessible={false}; escape on the sheet container); contract-enforced.

UI review: useScrollToEndOnKeyboard scrolls to the end whatever field is focused; on a very short viewport (iPhone SE, landscape, large Dynamic Type) focusing Email could scroll it out of view while typing. Not observed on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator; if it shows, scroll only for the password field. Android 'pan' + KeyboardAvoidingView interaction untested.

UI review: RegisterScreen and ForgotPasswordScreen use the same KeyboardAvoidingView + ScrollView pattern without the keyboard scroll; Register's later fields and submit can sit behind the keyboard until scrolled. Follow-up only: those forms are top-anchored, so the hook as written would be wrong for them.

Found by the insights-scope-select flow (pre-existing product behaviour, not changed): on the Insights tab, choosing a group that has no expenses replaces the screen with the 'No expenses in <month> yet' empty state, which has no 'Analyse' scope picker, so the user cannot switch back to 'My spending' from that screen. Needs a product decision (keep the scope control in the empty state).
UI review (pre-existing, not changed): Move-to-group, Recurring form/execute and RecurringPrompt modals have no onRequestClose, so the Android back gesture does nothing there.

Web/mobile parity gap found by the deep-link flows (not built here): the web app remembers an invite link across sign-in and resumes it (QA B-12); the mobile app has no pending-invite handling and JoinGroup exists only in the signed-in stack, so an invite opened while signed out is silently dropped and the user must reopen the link after signing in. Needs a product decision and a mobile change (persist the token, resume after sign-in).

Found by the receipt-import flow: an unanchored `rsync --exclude ios --exclude android` stripped modules/receipt-ocr/ios and /android from the e2e build clone, so e2e builds shipped WITHOUT on-device OCR and every receipt silently fell back to image upload (the app swallows OCR errors by design). FIXED: anchored excludes, guards that fail the build if the module folders are missing or ReceiptOcr is not in Podfile.lock, and the receipt-import flow asserts from the proxy log that parse_ocr was posted and the image was not uploaded (red before: no Vision code in the binary; green after). The Android APK guard (dex contains expo/modules/receiptocr) is written but unverified until the first Android build.

Code review: the fault proxy's request log was never reset, so lost-save-response and receipt-import counted requests from earlier flows and retries (a full run failed lost-save-response: 2 POSTs seen). FIXED: run_flows resets the proxy before every attempt; unit-tested; device-verified in a full run where expense-create ran before lost-save-response.

Code review: start-test-backend.sh's ERR trap aborted before cleanup when a child had already died (leaked Postgres + temp dir), and Ctrl-C/TERM left everything running. FIXED: `|| true` on the kills, INT/TERM trap running the same cleanup.

Code review: nothing gated flows by platform, so Android runs would fail date-picker and receipt-import deterministically. FIXED: `# PLATFORMS:` header honoured by run_flows; platform-skipped flows are reported SKIPPED, never as a pass. The Android variants of the two flows are NOT written (needs an Android run).

Code review: account-switch could pass vacuously (A's draft persistence never asserted; negative assertions ran before async loads). FIXED: kill/relaunch proves A's draft is restored first; a bounded settle wait precedes B's absence assertions.

Code review: seed.expect_proxy, the only guard for AC-005's 'exactly one POST' and 'no image upload', had no unit test. FIXED: tests for exact method/path matching, counts and fault counts, plus the proxy-reset and PROXY_CONTROL_URL hand-off.

Code review P3 batch, FIXED: weak final assertions in category-picker/insights-scope-select (now also assert the previous state is gone); run.sh exited silently without adb and attached to any running emulator (now only in CI or with E2E_REUSE_EMULATOR=1); android-emu.sh name validation, port-in-use check and boot timeout; build-android default arch from the host; Maestro timeouts now kill the whole process group; proxy tests use an HTTP/1.1 keep-alive backend and tear down cleanly; stale-clone hint; receipt fixture no longer carries a date that would age out.

Security review pass 3: the proxy control API had no Origin/Host/Content-Type checks, so a web page open on the dev machine could arm faults or clear the log (failed runs, no false pass). FIXED: 403 for any Origin or foreign Host, 415 for non-JSON POSTs; tested.

Security review pass 3 P3 batch, FIXED: stop script matches `fault_proxy.py --listen`; android-emu.sh refuses to take over a running emulator or a bad name; proxy has read timeouts, a bounded log, closes backend connections on error and survives oversized headers; ANDROID_USER_HOME redirected into the tools folder; seed.py reports JSON errors cleanly.

Product bug found by the first Android run: with the keyboard open the Sign in button was hidden behind it on Android and scrolling did nothing. app.json uses softwareKeyboardLayoutMode "pan", so the window pans instead of resizing, the ScrollView viewport does not shrink, the content never overflows and the iOS fix (scrollToEnd) had nothing to scroll. FIXED: useScrollToEndOnKeyboard returns {keyboardInset, onContentSizeChange}; on Android the keyboard height is reserved as bottom padding and the form re-scrolls once laid out; iOS is unchanged (inset 0). Failing-first Jest tests; login-relaunch passes on Android and iOS. Side effect noted for the UI reviewer: after a failed sign-in the scrolled-up email field is partly under the status bar and the error line is scrolled off. Verification: failing-first Jest tests for the inset and its release (mobile-unit-tests); device runs passed in about 44 of 45 Android sign-in screens, the residual is finding A-3.

Android emulator infrastructure: on a default pixel_6 AVD (2 GB, 2 cores, software rendering) adb dropped the device ('device offline' / 'device not found') during the first flows after boot, failing 4 of 16 flow starts. FIXED: AVD gets 4 GB and 4 cores, a stability check (5 consecutive good adb round trips) after boot, a readiness/reconnect check right before every Android flow, and a capped (2) infra retry from a fresh fixture that is recorded on the attempt and in summary.json (infra_retries) so it can never be mistaken for a clean pass. The final run had zero infra retries. Not yet proven on CI's x86_64 emulator. Verification: unit tests for device-loss detection, the capped infra retry, the DeviceGone abort and its record (framework-tests); the final run had zero infra retries.

Android receipt-OCR quality gap (cause not isolated): the on-device ML Kit module is in the app and runs (logcat: bundled latin model loaded from the APK; the app posts the text to POST /ingest/receipt/parse_ocr and does not upload the image), but for the synthetic fixtures/receipt.jpg the server's confidence is below OCR_LLM_FALLBACK_MIN_CONF (0.75), so the app takes the upload-fallback path and asks for AI consent instead of showing the items that Apple Vision's reading produces on iOS. Unknown whether this is the synthetic image, ML Kit's line confidences/geometry vs the server's grouping, or a real quality gap. The iOS flow (receipt-import) asserts the items; Android has receipt-ocr-native-android, which proves only that native OCR ran and nothing was uploaded without consent. Next step: capture ML Kit's lines for a real receipt on a physical Android device (stays a manual check) and compare with the server's group_rows/confidence.

Code review (reproduced): an attempt that raised (seed.provision failure, adb timeout, DeviceGone) produced a result without a `dir`, and device_lost() raised KeyError, killing the whole run and losing the remaining flows: the exact adb-lost scenario the infra retry targets. FIXED test-first: device_lost tolerates a missing dir, the attempt is recorded as a failed attempt with its error.

Code + security review (same finding): receipt-ocr-native-android claimed 'zero image uploads after declining the AI prompt', but uploadReceipt always POSTs to /ingest/receipt/parse?allow_ai=<choice> on our own server and the SERVER enforces allow_ai=false, so the claim was wrong, and the check ran before the proxy had logged an in-flight request (it could pass vacuously). FIXED: the proxy log now keeps the allow_ai query value (and nothing else from the query) and also logs requests the backend never answered; the verify waits 5 s, then asserts exactly one parse_ocr and at most one /parse, every one with allow_ai=false; headers and docs state the real contract.

Code review: after the emulator failed to return, every later flow waited 90 s again (about 20 min for 13 flows) and the cause was buried. FIXED: DeviceGone aborts the run; the in-flight flow is recorded failed and the rest as `not_run` (never a pass, makes the run fail).

Security/code review P3 batch, FIXED: the proxy refuses ambiguous request framing (duplicate Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding, non-chunked or combined Transfer-Encoding) instead of forwarding it; run.sh no longer runs `stop` (which kills emulator-5580) when `start` refused because someone else's emulator holds the port (exit 3); the emulator log moved from a predictable shared-temp name to the gitignored .build folder; android-emu.sh derives the image architecture from the host and waits for the device to disappear before deleting the AVD (and warns if it cannot); Ctrl-C/SIGTERM to the runner now kills the Maestro process group; the cleartext comment/AGENTS wording says 'app-wide in e2e binaries, API origin pinned by baseUrl.ts' (the manifest cannot scope it to one host); a test joins run_flows.reset_proxy and seed.proxy_log to the real proxy (Host/Origin/JSON checks).

USER_PASSWORD is passed to Maestro with -e on its command line and is visible in `ps` for the flow's duration. Accepted: the user is created per flow in a disposable database that exists only for the run, on loopback. Proposed for acceptance; it needs the repository owner's waiver (owner, reason, reference, expiry) before it can be marked accepted. Not a gate blocker (P3).

UI review: with the keyboard open the sign-in form is scrolled to its end, so the email field being typed into can sit under the status bar (confirmed in the Android run; likely on iOS too since scrollToEnd is shared; worse on small screens/large fonts). WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured. Fix: scroll to min(end offset, form top minus the top inset) or scroll on the focused field's onFocus. The E2E flows assert the Sign in button for this reason.

UI review (pre-existing, shared UI outside this change): the toast that shows 'Login failed' has no live-region role or announcement, so TalkBack/VoiceOver users may not hear it. Fix: accessibilityLiveRegion polite/assertive + accessibilityRole alert on core/ui/Toast.tsx. Needs a real screen-reader check.

UI/code review: only API 35 was exercised. (a) KeyboardAvoidingView behavior='height' stays on Android and the new keyboard inset is added on top, so on API < 35 or non-edge-to-edge setups the form may get about twice the keyboard height of padding (landscape: Sign in could scroll off); (b) the inset can be stale if keyboardDidHide is missed (backgrounding, rotation, multi-window); (c) endCoordinates.height may include the nav-bar inset or be wrong in split-screen/foldables; (d) scrollToEnd while TalkBack is moving focus may fight it. Verify on API 29-34, landscape, a Samsung device and TalkBack; consider behavior={undefined} on Android.

Android sign-in keyboard fix (A-1) is not 100% reliable: in the final full Android run (and10) deep-link-signed-out failed once because Sign in stayed hidden behind the keyboard (screenshot identical to the original bug); it had passed in about 44 earlier Android sign-in screens since the fix. Cause not isolated (keyboard event racing layout is the leading hypothesis: the form was not scrolled although the keyboard was up). MITIGATED, not diagnosed, by owner decision to avoid more device runs: on Android the hook now repeats the scroll at +120 ms and +400 ms after the keyboard opens (cancelled by hide/unmount; iOS untouched), covered by unit tests. The re-scroll is NOT device-verified; the CI Android runs will show whether the flake recurs (a recurrence is reported as FLAKY with the first failure kept). If it recurs: run the 30-iteration sign-in loop with keyboard-event logging.

Security review (reproduced in a scratch repo): the CI classifier read changed files with `git diff --name-only`, which C-quotes non-ASCII or unusual names (`"varavu_selavu_mobile/src/\303\251.ts"`), so the prefix match failed and a PR whose only mobile change had such a name skipped the device jobs while `Native mobile gate` passed. FIXED: `git diff -z --name-only --no-renames` split on NUL; a regression test builds a real git repo with a non-ASCII, a tab and a quote in names and asserts they are all seen as mobile changes.

Security review: under `pull_request` the PR's own copy of mobile-e2e.yml and mobile_e2e_gate.py runs, so a PR could weaken its own gate (the post-merge push run uses main's code, and both files are in MOBILE_AFFECTING_FILES). This is true of every workflow in the repo. Mitigation is organisational: a CODEOWNERS file for .github/workflows/, scripts/quality/ and qa/mobile/ with required code-owner review in the ruleset (no CODEOWNERS exists today).

UI review: the Android re-scroll delays (120/400 ms) are guesses and are not device-verified, so on a slow device the race could still occur; forced scrolls can also fight TalkBack focus for up to 400 ms (a marginal worsening of F-018 d). A more deterministic design would scroll from onLayout or an effect on keyboardInset, and skip the timers when a screen reader is on (AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled). The E2E assertion on the Sign in button stays as the safety net.

Code review pass 5: the release gate's 'dispatch a regression run' hint appeared only when no mobile-e2e.yml run existed; since the workflow starts on every push to main and skips the device jobs when nothing mobile changed, the usual case is a run with skipped jobs and the gate blocked without saying what to do. FIXED: the hint is appended whenever the mobile evidence fails; tested for no-run, skipped-jobs and the passing case (no hint). Same pass, P3s FIXED: SIGTERM now unwinds like Ctrl-C so Maestro is never orphaned; an aborted flow keeps its real attempts and infra-retry count (plus the reason the run stopped); a test drives main() through the abort branch; the emulator serial match is anchored to a whole word. These post-review fixes are covered by unit tests and were not re-reviewed.
